new_statements.quote: p.15: '4. ACCENT In order to obtain a good pronunciation of these languages, especially of Ndogo, great attention must be paid to the accent. The following suggestions (I shall not call them rules) may serve as a guide for Ndogo. ... III. The most noteworthy difference in accent exists among words of two syllables, some having an even stress on both syllables, and some having a real accent on the first. ... V. Bviri. Most of the remarks made for Ndogo hold good.' p.29: '(d) As hinted above (5. iv.), the accent usually lies on the first syllable of dissyllables: thus, in reduplication, accents lie on the first and third syllables.' p.8: 'II. Bai ... This language wavers between Ndogo and Bviri. Generally speaking it follows closely the former.'

new_statements.rule_in_words: Group-level (Ndogo-modelled) accent sketch for the Ndogo-Sere-Tagbu-Bai-Bviri languages: monosyllables unproblematic; polysyllables are mostly compounds and each component keeps its own accent; in dissyllables the accent 'usually lies on the first syllable' (clearly so when the second syllable has l, r, n; other dissyllables have 'even stress' on both syllables); reduplicated dissyllables are accented on syllables 1 and 3. The languages are tonal (sec. 5, four pitch levels). Nothing is said about accent in Bai specifically; Bai is stated to follow Ndogo closely, and the Ndogo remarks are said to hold for Bviri.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not treated as such; compounds and reduplications carry an accent on each component (syllables 1 and 3 in reduplicated dissyllables).
new_statements.exceptions: Dissyllables without l/r/n in the second syllable have 'even stress on both syllables'; reduplication mbulambula accented on the second syllable of each component; predicative adjectives/verbs with lengthened final vowel take the 'accent on the doubled vowel' (p. 26); with r in the second syllable that syllable is often lost (mboro = mboo, koro = koo).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level pronunciation guidance for isolated words (author calls them 'suggestions', not rules), framed for the whole group with Ndogo as the model; Bai only covered by implication (p. 8 'follows closely' Ndogo). Text accessed as verbatim Google Books snippets, not continuous pages; remark V (Bviri) continuation and any further Bai detail not recovered.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted accent statement is a group-level sketch in a comparative grammar of Ndogo-Sere-Tagbu-Bai-Bviri, explicitly modelled on Ndogo (ndog1248) and explicitly extended to Bviri (Belanda Viri, bela1255); Bai (baii1251, bdj) is not named in the accent section and is covered only via p. 8 'This language wavers between Ndogo and Bviri. Generally speaking it follows closely the former.' Not to be confused with the Sino-Tibetan Bai of Yunnan (full-text hits for 'Bai language stress' are all that language).
